findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The standing cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. The following TCS food items were probed and were observed to be above 41F: 

1. A container of bleu cheese dressing probed to be at 54F. 
2. A container of salsa probed to be at 61F. 
3. A container of tartar sauce probed to be at 57F. 
4. A container of thousand island dressing probed to be at 56F. 
5. A container of honey mustard probed to be at 60F. 

CORRECTED- The sauces were voluntarily discarded by an employee. It was discussed to not store any more TCS foods in the cooler until it is repaired and cold holding at 41F and under.  Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The standing cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. The owner is still waiting on a part to come in so the cooler can be repaired. A follow up is scheduled for 8/5/2026 to ensure that the cooler has been repaired and is properly cold holding at 41F and below.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
There is not an ingredient list that includes allergens on the cooler containing the grab and go cheesecake slices. CORRECTED- The PIC sent a photo of a list of ingredients and allergens for the cheesecakes that has been posted on the outside of the cooler. Ensure that food items that are packaged for consumer grab and go are properly labeled. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the back of house hand washing sink being used to thaw fish. CORRECTED- the pan was removed from the sink and education was conducted with employees. Hand washing sinks must be used for hand washing ONLY. Cease this practice.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the following temperature control for food safety (TCS) items stored in the non-operational standing cooler: ranch, blue cheese, thousand island dressing, and French dressing (all labeled either “Refrigerate after opening, or keep Refrigerated”- this categorization indicates that the foods are TCS). Blue cheese (stated to have been in the cooler the longest) was observed to have an internal temperature of 56F. The toppings labeled  “refrigerate after opening” in the countertop cooler were also observed at 45F.  CORRECTED- items in the cheesecake cooler were moved to the walk in cooler, and items in the dessert topping station were moved to the front. All cold held TCS foods must be held under 41F. The temperature danger zone is 41-135F. Pathogens that cause food-borne illness proliferate in this temperature range.

The PIC stated the item is under warranty and they are waiting on a part. Do NOT store any TCS foods (including those labeled “Refrigerate after opening”) in this cooler until it is fixed. The ambient temperature was observed to be 52F. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/20/26.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two uncovered drinks in the kitchen. CORRECTED- education was conducted and drinks were removed from food prep area to be covered. Ensure personal drinks are in a designated space, and have a lid and straw to prevent potential contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the ice scoop handle touching ice in the ice machine. CORRECTED- the scoop was removed for ware washing. Ensure ready to eat foods (consumables such as ice) are handled with utensils that have handles, that do NOT make contact with food products. Scoops must either be stored in a way that the scoop is stored separate from the food, or sticking outwards so as not to touch the food products, to prevent bare hand contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 5 dented cans of mushrooms (X4) and tomato sauce (X1) in dry storage. CORRECTED- education was conducted regarding dented cans, and the items were removed from service to be returned to the supplier for credit. Large dents along the body, and ANY dents along the seams may allow for the growth and harborage of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods to contain an internal temperature between 48-52F in the dessert topping cooler and the back room cheesecake cooler. Foods include, but are not limited to strawberry topping labeled “refrigerate after opening” (48-49F), and sour cream (52F). CORRECTED- items in the countertop dessert cooler were switched (items in the front are non-TCS, and are probing within acceptable range). Items in the standing dessert cooler were moved to the walk in cooling units. Ensure all TCS items are held 41F, or time as control (TAC) is implemented, with the items to be used or discarded within 4 hours.

findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris and limescale along the baffles of the ice machine. The person in charge (PIC) took a picture of the baffles and ensured the inspector they will be cleaned in a timely manner. Discussed periodically defrosting the ice machine to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may migrate into ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items in the counter top cooler (next to the drive thru window) to be above 41F. Sour cream, tartar sauce, and ranch were stored in a unit with an ambient temperature between 48-52F. Sour cream was probed to have an internal temperature of 48, ranch was probed to have an internal temperature of 52F, and tartar sauce was probed to have an internal temperature above 41F. The PIC showed the inspector the container from which the sauces were removed, and they all indicated “Refrigerate after opening.” CORRECTED- the PIC instructed kitchen staff to pack the aforementioned items to be discarded. They also stated that sauces will be stored in the milk cooler unit the unit is serviced or replaced. Ensure all TCS foods are cold held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple cooling units to be lacking ambient thermometers (whole cheesecake standing cooler, counter top cooler, prep coolers). Inspector informed the PIC that the digital temperature read out displays temperature at the coldest part of the unit. To ensure safety of TCS foods, cold holding units (with the exception of freezers) should also contain ambient thermometers to ensure that the warmest part of the unit is at or below 41F. Inspector will check for ambient thermometers during the 1/26 follow up inspection due to violations #22 and #33.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: The inspector observed staff handling diced tomatoes with bare hands. Discussed with PIC, and the tomatoes in question were discarded. Ensure that staff are made aware to wear gloves during food preparation at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(E)(2) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE POPULATION may contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands if: (2) Written procedures are maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request that include: (a) For each bare hand contact procedure, a listing of the specific READY-TO-EAT FOODS that are touched by bare hands, (b) Diagrams and other information showing that handwashing facilities, installed, located, equipped, and maintained as specified under §§ 5-203.11, 5-204.11, 5-205.11, 6-301.11, 6-301.12, and 6-301.14, are in an easily accessible location and in close proximity to the work station where the bare hand contact procedure is conducted.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: The inspector observed chicken being stored over fish in the double-door stainless steel cooler in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC, and the fish was removed to correct the storage order violation. Ensure that raw food items are stored properly to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine were observed with a build-up of soil. Discussed with PIC, who ensured the inspector that the ice machine baffles will be cleaned in the coming week. Ensure that food-contact surfaces, such as the baffles of the ice machine, are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-202.11(A) Restriction. (A) Only those POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS that are required for the operation and maintenance of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as for the cleaning and SANITIZING of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS and the control of insects and rodents, shall be allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

A couple chemical canisters were observed to be improperly stored over food items. 
-1 stainless steel refrigerator cleaner canister
-1 glass cleaner canister 
Discussed with PIC, and the canisters were removed and stored away properly. Ensure that staff are aware of the storage order of toxic chemicals and food items to avoid food contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the caulking on the countertop on the right of the dish machine to be in disrepair. Discussed with PIC, who ensured the inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the countertop is re-caulked to the wall, providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand-sink in the kitchen was observed to be out of paper towels. Discussed with PIC that every hand sink is required to have adequate paper towels available. Towels were added to the dispenser. Ensure that relevant drying disposable towels are available at all times.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-202.11(A) Restriction. (A) Only those POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS that are required for the operation and maintenance of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as for the cleaning and SANITIZING of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS and the control of insects and rodents, shall be allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

A series of chemical canisters were observed to be improperly stored over food items. 
-7 stainless steel refrigerator cleaner canisters
-1air freshener canister
-1 RAID insecticide canister above the tortilla wraps
Discussed with PIC and the canisters were removed and stored away properly. Ensure that staff are aware of the storage order of toxic chemicals and food items to avoid food contamination.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

Two boxes of chicken were observed to be sitting on the counter top next to the hand sink in the dry storage area at the beginning of the inspection and remained there for over an hour. Discussed with PIC and the boxes were to be taken to the fridge for storage. Ensure that appropriate thawing method is used for food items.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT X2) 3-304.14 (B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).
 
Wiping cloths were observed to be out of sanitizer solution.The rags were placed in a bucket of sanitizer solution to correct. Ensure that cloths used for wiping counters and food contact surfaces are stored between uses in a solution of adequate concentration.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11(B) Kitchenware and Tableware. (B) Knives, forks, and spoons that are not pre-wrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and by CONSUMERS if CONSUMER self service is provided.

Single used utensils were observed to be stored out of order. Discussed with PIC and the PIC ensured the inspectors that the utensils will be rearranged to their proper order. Ensure that single service utensils are stored in the order where only the handles are touched to avoid contamination of the food contact areas. Items were adjusted during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips were observed to be absent during and at the end of the inspection. Discussed with PIC and the PIC ensured that they had them but may have fallen somewhere. Ensure that test strips are available at all time to have an adequate reading on sanitizer solution concentration.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mop is observed stored with the head on the floor in the kitchen next to the sink. Mop storage has been an ongoing issue at this facility. The PIC was shown and moved the mop to proper storage by the mop sink to correct. Ensure that the mop heads are stored between uses so that the bristles are able to hang and drip dry.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: At the start of the inspection, a wiping cloth was observed stored on the surface of the prep table. This cloth was removed from this location and placed into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure the wiping cloths are stored submerged in the sanitizer bucket between uses.
This is a repeat violation from the 4/2/24 inspection and the facility will receive a Warning Notice to document this violation. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: In the utility sink room and in the kitchen, the mops were observed to be stored on the floor and not able to air dry. The mops were inverted/hung up during the inspection. Ensure after use that mops are placed in a position that allows for air drying without posing a contamination hazard with their placement. This is a repeat violation from the 4/2/24 inspection and the facility will receive a Warning Notice to document this violation. 
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor under the triple sink/dish washing area is observed to have an accumulation of food soils/debris. Ensure that cleaning takes place to remove the current accumulation.
